title: Console calibration job lifecycle: orchestration, artifacts retention, and RBAC for quantization validation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a first-class calibration job orchestration experience in Redwood Console focused on FP8/INT8 quantization profiles and automated accuracy validation. The feature should let teams run calibration jobs, inspect artifacts (calibration tables, reports, golden-run comparisons), set retention policies, and control access per-org and per-team. This ticket sculpts UX and product requirements for the initial implementation and defines roll-out phases.
background: Customers performing quantization rely on calibration runs to compute activation ranges/scale factors and to validate accuracy regressions versus float baselines. Currently calibration is ad-hoc (CLI + S3) and lacks discoverability, retention management, and RBAC in Console. We need a managed orchestration flow to reduce failure modes, improve auditability, and provide clear artifacts for QA and post-deploy comparisons.
goals: Provide a Console-first flow to create and monitor calibration jobs (FP8/INT8), view run artifacts and metrics
Expose calibration artifacts (profile JSONs, calibration histograms, evaluation diffs) via Console links and pre-signed downloads
Configurable artifact retention policy per-job and org default; enterprise override for long-term retention
Enforce RBAC for job creation, artifact access, and audit logging
Include automated accuracy validation: run eval harness against a golden prompt set and surface regression flags
non_goals: Full offline bulk calibration orchestration in phase 1 (we will support single-run jobs and scheduled jobs later)
Replacing low-level CLI workflows in the first release; we will integrate the CLI after API APIs stabilize
Automatic model re-quantization rollouts into production (out of scope; only produces artifacts and recommendations)
success_metrics: >50% of internal calibration runs performed via Console within 60 days of launch
Reduction in support tickets related to 'lost calibration artifacts' by 80%
<5% calibration jobs end in non-actionable failure (missing artifacts) after platform improvements
Customers can detect accuracy regressions via Console alerts in <5 min from run completion
acceptance_criteria: Create Calibration Job modal with required fields: model (name + version), dataset reference, quant profile (FP8/INT8), calibration strategy (minmax/kl), batch_size, target_accuracy_threshold
Jobs create a run entry (queued -> running -> succeeded/failed/cancelled) visible in Console Runs table
Artifacts produced: calibration_profile.json, calibration_histograms.png, eval_report.json, sample_inference_diffs.json and stored under structured artifact path
Retention UI allows setting per-job TTL (days) and shows org default; artifacts are deleted after TTL when not configured for long-retention

RBAC rules: 'Calibration Creator' can create/cancel; 'Calibration Operator' can run/retry/cancel; 'Calibration Viewer' can view metrics and download reports; raw binary tensors require explicit 'artifact_download' permission
Audit log entries created for job create/cancel/download with timestamps and actor
Automated accuracy validation compares eval_report.json against baseline and marks run with PASS/WARN/FAIL using configurable thresholds
design_notes: Modal flow should reuse existing Console patterns: left-aligned form, searchable model selector with pinned versions, dataset selector that supports internal dataset ids and external GCS/S3 URIs. Runs table includes quick filters (status, model, quant profile, owner). Artifacts list shows compact badges for file type and size with 'View' and 'Download'. Retention control is a dropdown with options (7d, 30d, 90d, 365d, indefinite[enterprise]).
orchestration_requirements: Backend job scheduler supports priorities and per-org concurrency limits
Retries: exponential backoff with max 3 retries for transient infra errors
Cancellation should trigger a graceful stop and partial artifact upload with a run status 'cancelled' and partial artifacts preserved according to retention policy
Auto-fallback: if INT8 calibration fails due to numeric issues, optionally rerun using FP8 or fallback to FP16 path depending on user preference
Pinning: job must record exact model artifact SHA and tokenizer version to ensure reproducibility
retention_policy_details: Default org retention: 90 days. Users may override per-job TTL at creation. Enterprise customers may enable 'long-term retention' (365+ days) with archived storage class. Deletion is a soft-delete for 30 days (recoverable) then hard-delete. Console shows 'expires on' date per artifact. Admins can export a retention report for compliance audits.
permissions_model: Role: calibration_creator => can create jobs, set retention up to org-max limit, view and download artifacts
Role: calibration_operator => can start/stop/retry jobs, view logs, cannot change org-wide defaults
Role: calibration_viewer => read-only access to run metadata, can view aggregated metrics but requires artifact_download permission to download raw files
Admin override => org admins can configure policy that prevents downloads of raw tensors outside secure buckets
Audit logs => all mutation events (create/cancel/download/modify-retention) recorded with actor_id, timestamp, IP
api_contracts: POST /api/v1/calibrations -> create job. Body must include model_id, model_sha, dataset_uri, quant_profile (FP8|INT8), strategy, target_accuracy, retention_days
GET /api/v1/calibrations/:job_id/artifacts -> list artifacts with pre-signed URLs (expires 15m)
ui_flow: 1) User opens 'New Calibration Job' in Console. 2) Select model/version, dataset, quant profile, and eval suite. 3) Optionally toggle 'auto-validate accuracy' and set threshold. 4) Submit; job appears in Runs table. 5) When job completes, Console surfaces PASS/WARN/FAIL and links to artifacts and eval diff viewer.
monitoring_and_alerts: Emit metrics: calibration.job.started, calibration.job.completed, calibration.job.failed, calibration.artifact.upload_errors. Create alerts: >10% job failure rate in 1h window; artifact upload error spikes. Integrate with Console notifications and email for org admins when critical failures occur.
testing_plan: Unit tests for API input validation (missing model_sha, invalid retention_days)
Integration test with S3 emulator to verify artifact upload and pre-signed URL generation
E2E manual QA: create jobs across FP8/INT8, confirm eval_report PASS/WARN/FAIL logic against synthetic baseline datasets
Security review: ensure pre-signed URLs respect RBAC and cannot be generated without proper permission
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): surface create/run UI, artifact listing, default retention, basic RBAC (creator/operator/viewer) for internal orgs. Phase 2: enterprise retention settings, admin retention reports, audit export. Phase 3: scheduled recurring calibration, integration with Redwood Optimize recommendations and console-driven re-quantization runbooks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Large artifacts overflow storage and increase costs -> Mitigation: enforce per-org artifact size limits and default to compressed JSON/PNG, tiered storage for archived artifacts
Risk: Users accidentally leak raw tensors -> Mitigation: restrict raw tensor downloads to secure buckets and require explicit 'artifact_download' permission; log all downloads
Risk: Calibration runs consume disproportionate GPU capacity -> Mitigation: per-org concurrency quotas and job priority system; admin can set daily quotas
updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Design, and Security. Agreed scope for MVP and enterprise features.
2026-02-24: Eng completed spike comparing storage options (S3 vs internal blobstore); recommend S3 with lifecycle rules and soft-delete layer.
2026-03-01: API contract drafted; initial server-side schema PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/api#456).
2026-03-05: Design provided first-pass mocks for Runs table and artifact drawer; UX review scheduled.
2026-03-10: Security reviewed pre-signed URL approach; requires token-bound URL and RBAC check in signing service. Updated acceptance criteria accordingly.
notes_for_engineers: Ensure runs capture reproducibility metadata: model SHA, tokenizer version, calibration seed, dataset snapshot id. Use content-addressable paths for calibration_profile.json and include checksums in metadata. Implement hook to record eval baseline SHA and store eval_report.json with both raw metrics and per-prompt diffs.
final_comment: This ticket captures the product requirements and acceptance criteria necessary for an MVP of Console-based calibration orchestration. Engineering should prioritize reproducibility, RBAC, and auditability. After MVP, we will iterate quickly on retention ergonomics and Optimize integration.
